summary: This Docusaurus plugin builds a searchable index of questions extracted from blog articles. It reads question sidecars (pre-generated JSON files paired with each article), deduplicates them across the corpus, and outputs the index in three different formats optimized for different consumers: a small summary for the FAQ hub, individual theme-specific routes for code-splitting, and a full JSON file for client-side search.

explanations.58: fs.readdirSync() reads directory contents synchronously; the withFileTypes option returns objects with metadata (like isDirectory()) instead of just filenames.
explanations.61: The spread operator (...) unpacks the nested array from the recursive call into the parent array, flattening all results into one list.
explanations.74: This checks if the article's front-matter has an explicit slug field; if it does, use that as the URL path; otherwise fall back to a directory-based URL.
explanations.86: normalize('NFD') decomposes accented characters into base letters plus separate accent marks — so 'é' becomes 'e' plus an accent mark.
explanations.87: The \p{M} regex matches combining marks (accents, diacritics); removing them leaves just the base letters, which is how 'café' becomes 'cafe'.
explanations.101: A Map is created to count how many times each normalized question text appears across all articles.
explanations.104: For each entry, we look up its normalized question text in the counts map, get the current count (or 0 if new), and increment it.
explanations.107: filter() keeps only entries where the normalized question appears exactly once; if a question appears twice, both instances are removed.
explanations.119: This ternary returns the blog directory path — either the main blog folder for the default locale, or the translated copy nested under i18n.
explanations.125: If the blog directory doesn't exist yet (no articles), return early with empty results rather than crashing.
explanations.132: frontMatter() parses the YAML header at the top of a markdown file and returns an object with an attributes field containing the key-value pairs.
explanations.137: A sidecar file is expected to live alongside the article with the same path plus .questions.json appended.
explanations.142: JSON.parse() converts the file's text content into a JavaScript object; the try-catch silently skips any sidecar that's invalid JSON.
explanations.152: path.relative() computes the folder path from the blog root to the article; split/join converts Windows backslashes to forward slashes for URLs.
explanations.180: yaml.load() converts YAML text into a JavaScript object; the ?? operator returns an empty object if the result is null or undefined.
explanations.203: new Map() creates a key-value store where the key is the article's mainTag and the value is an array of all questions with that tag.
explanations.216: If the key is 'other' (articles with no mainTag), look up the localized label; otherwise use the label from the tags.yml file.
explanations.260: mkdirSync with recursive: true creates the directory and any missing parent directories without throwing an error if they already exist.
explanations.263: JSON.stringify(entries) converts the array of question objects to JSON text; this plain file is served as an HTTP asset, not bundled into JavaScript.
explanations.269: actions.createData() registers a data file that Docusaurus will bundle; await ensures the file is written before we reference it in the next step.
explanations.276: normalizeUrl() concatenates URL segments into a single route path, handling leading/trailing slashes; baseUrl ensures the route works under non-English locales.
